The residual is dominated by a single root cause, not scattered bugs: this compiler puts `work` in a hard callee-saved register (fp initially, r9 after moving `frame`'s initialization earlier and switching the outer loop from `for` to `while` -- a source-shape change that measurably helped, 472->458 differing_halfwords) instead of reference's scheme of never hard-registering `work` (always reloaded from its sp+40 stack slot, confirmed by grepping every `ldr r?, [sp, #40]` site in the reference disassembly, even deep inside the triply-nested particle-draw loop) and always keeping `frame` in fp for the whole function. Bisected this by wrapping first the per-member event loop and then the particle-table draw block in `#if 0` and re-measuring: removing the member loop alone flips `work` from fp to r9 (still wrong, just a different hard register); removing the particle block alone leaves `work` on fp; neither isolates a single offending statement, confirming this is a whole-function global-register-allocation-priority effect, not a local one. This is the exact same open, cross-family, evidence-exhausted residual documented at length in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json (fifth pass), 080d59b0.json (fifth pass), and especially 080e01e4.json (fourth pass, note (b)) for this same 0x03001eec work-block family -- those three dossiers record roughly a dozen combined targeted attempts (declaration order, block scoping, identifier renaming away from the ARM register mnemonic, accumulator-shape variants, loop-shape variants) that had zero or negative effect on which persistent local lands in which callee-saved register. Applied the two cheap, already-established levers from that precedent here too: merged the particle-draw loop's counter identity into the already block-scoped `i` (mirroring 080e01e4's successful n->i merge) -- zero measured effect, consistent with that finding generalizing; and moved `frame = 0` earlier plus a for->while conversion -- this one *did* help (472->458), unlike the family's other declaration-order experiments, but did not resolve the underlying register-role swap (work still ends up hard-registered instead of stack-spilled). Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect that alpha-blend-fades in and back out (BLDALPHA at 0x04000052) over an 80-frame run. Seeds a 16-entry randomized particle table at work+0x7080, registers a single finish callback, then per frame: computes a sine-derived 'wave' offset, occasionally clears a canvas region via an indirect call through a runtime function pointer at 0x03000168, updates the alpha-blend register during the fade edges, and -- when the object's mode-select field chooses a non-zero table row -- draws three fixed sprites plus up to four active entries from the particle table at positions derived from sine/cosine of a per-particle-group angle. Independently, whenever frame crosses one of seven per-member thresholds it cues two member-specific presentation calls (Func_080d6888/Func_080b5088).

The dominant open residual is a whole-function register-allocation-priority question (which persistent local this compiler's allocator puts in fp vs r9 vs stack) that is already documented at length as evidence-exhausted for this exact 0x03001eec work-block family across three other siblings (080dc1ec.json, 080d59b0.json, 080e01e4.json); this dossier's score.note records this owner's own bisection evidence and the two established levers re-tried here (one helped modestly, one had zero effect, matching the family's mixed-result pattern for this class of issue).
